headline: Carbon capture pitched as a "game changer" for Brunei
summary: A TradeWinds feature from Brunei Darussalam Maritime Week argues carbon capture and liquefied-CO2 shipping could reshape the sultanate's economy, positioning Brunei as a prospective regional CO2 storage-and-shipping hub. No capacity or investment figures disclosed.
co2crc_note: Another APAC state eyeing a CO2 shipping-and-storage hub role sharpens the regional competition Australia's export-storage ambitions sit within.
extractor_note: Trade-press strategy/positioning feature, not a firm commitment; only headline/metadata accessible (paywall).

headline: Rotork manufactures first IQ3 Pro actuators for the Liverpool Bay carbon capture project
summary: Supplier Rotork produced the first of its IQ3 Pro electric actuators for the Liverpool Bay CO2 transport-and-storage system (Eni's repurposed depleted gas fields, part of the HyNet North West cluster), an early procurement-and-fabrication milestone. No contract value disclosed.
co2crc_note: Supply-chain progress signal on a UK Track-1 T&S project; marginal direct relevance to CO2CRC beyond confirming HyNet build momentum.
extractor_note: Supplier equipment fabrication milestone; no contract value disclosed.

headline: An oil field became California's first carbon vault - who's responsible if something goes wrong?
summary: A CalMatters investigation into Carbon TerraVault I (California Resources Corp's Elk Hills project, the state's first operational CO2 store) probes long-term stewardship and liability for stored CO2 and notes California has yet to finalise the CCS rules its own law requires.
co2crc_note: Long-term liability and stewardship for permanent storage is the same social-licence question Australian offshore storage (Otway, CarbonNet, Bayu-Undan) must answer.

headline: KAIST and MIT turn seawater CO2 into "stone" for permanent storage
summary: KAIST (Dong-Yeun Koh) with MIT's T. Alan Hatton group unveiled an electrochemical dissolved-ocean-carbon (e-DOC) process converting seawater-dissolved CO2 into solid calcium carbonate for durable storage; published in Advanced Energy Materials, funded partly by Hyundai Motor and Kia.
co2crc_note: Early-stage marine-CDR/mineralisation science; watch-item for the durable-removal technology landscape rather than a near-term CO2CRC pathway.
extractor_note: Radar / near-miss: underlying study dated 4 Aug 2026, outside the 10-11 Aug window; peer-reviewed primary citation (Advanced Energy Materials).

headline: Drax secures Environment Agency permit variation for Selby BECCS
summary: The UK Environment Agency granted Drax an environmental permit variation to add bioenergy-with-CCS at its Selby biomass plant, clearing captured CO2 to be piped for permanent North Sea storage - a regulatory milestone for one of the UK's largest proposed CCS projects.
co2crc_note: A regulator permitting BECCS at scale is a live precedent for negative-emissions permitting and long-term storage governance relevant to Australian CCS/BECCS policy.
extractor_note: Radar / near-miss: published 7 Aug 2026, three days outside the 10-11 Aug window.
